真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 17 页

原文与作答 · 分开滚动

原文第1段Gwendoline (1882-1951) and Margaret (1884-1963) Davies were the granddaughters of David Davies, a Welshman who amassed a fortune in the shipping and mining industries. In 1907, when Gwendoline came into her inheritance (Margaret would follow in 1909), the sisters were said to be the wealthiest unmarried women in Britain. Their religious upbringing in rural Wales gave them a deep sense of social responsibility and they chose to use their inheritance for cultural and philanthropic* purposes.

原文第2段While there was no real family history of art collecting, the sisters' education was rigorously geared toward such pursuits. Their London school focused on cultural rather than academic study, and they travelled extensively with their governess, Jane Blaker, visiting art galleries and making extensive notes on the collections there.

原文第3段The sisters began to make regular art purchases from 1908, which roughly coincided with the dates of their inheritance. They took advice from various people, including the art dealer Hugh Blaker (the brother of Jane Blaker) and David Croal Thompson, who was also an art dealer. While it was long assumed that these men were largely responsible for the nature of the sisters' collection, it has recently been accepted that Gwendoline and Margaret retained a far more active role in the process.

原文第4段The sisters' journals reveal their preference for Old Master** paintings. Yet they initially made very few attempts to secure any such works. While the sisters were wealthy in relative terms, their income was nothing compared to the fortunes of American art collectors of this period, such as J. Pierpont Morgan. Quite simply, high quality Old Master works were, if not beyond their means, then beyond what they were willing to pay for them. Instead, their early purchases were of the fashionable, safe variety, and included, for example, paintings by the French artist Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot.

* philanthropic: seeking to promote the welfare of others, often by charitable funding

** Old Master: a highly respected artist of great skill who worked in Europe before about 1800

题目与作答

Q1–4：Complete the notes. Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer. Q8：TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN。原题号保留。

1. Family and early life: their grandfather's wealth came from 1 __________ and transportation businesses

2. their 2 __________ was designed to give them an interest in activities such as collecting art

3. they took lengthy 3 __________ about the things they saw in art galleries

4. their 4 __________ showed they liked Old Master paintings, but they were expensive to buy

8. The Davies sisters' childhood influenced the way they decided to use their wealth.

对照答案，回到证据

第 1 题 · mining

transportation对应shipping；and并列的另一行业是mining。答案限一词。

a fortune in the shipping and mining industries

第 2 题 · education

designed to give them an interest是was geared toward的改写，主语为education。

the sisters' education was rigorously geared toward such pursuits

第 3 题 · notes

lengthy对应extensive；took notes对应making notes，保留复数。

making extensive notes on the collections there

第 4 题 · journals

showed they liked对应reveal their preference；注意不能把其他段落的notes填进来。

The sisters' journals reveal their preference for Old Master

第 8 题 · TRUE

童年教养产生社会责任感，下一分句明确说因此把遗产用于文化及慈善，完整因果支持题干。

Their religious upbringing in rural Wales gave them a deep sense of social responsibility

核对原答案页

材料精读 · 内容与词句

这一部分把姐妹收藏艺术的起点放回家庭财富、成长教育与个人选择中理解：遗产提供条件，社会责任感影响用途，文化教育培养兴趣；她们听取顾问意见，却也有自己的判断。最后一段进一步说明，有购买能力、有个人偏好和愿意支付某个价格，是三个不同层面。

原文第1段

Gwendoline (1882-1951) and Margaret (1884-1963) Davies were the granddaughters of David Davies, a Welshman who amassed a fortune in the shipping and mining industries. In 1907, when Gwendoline came into her inheritance (Margaret would follow in 1909), the sisters were said to be the wealthiest unmarried women in Britain. Their religious upbringing in rural Wales gave them a deep sense of social responsibility and they chose to use their inheritance for cultural and philanthropic* purposes.

姐妹的财富来自祖父经营航运和采矿积累的资产，两人分别在1907年和1909年继承遗产。文中用were said to be转述她们当时被认为是英国最富有的未婚女性，而不是给出精确财富排名。宗教教养和威尔士乡村成长环境使她们产生社会责任感，因此她们选择把钱用于文化和慈善。财富来源与财富用途在这里被连接起来。

原文第2段

While there was no real family history of art collecting, the sisters' education was rigorously geared toward such pursuits. Their London school focused on cultural rather than academic study, and they travelled extensively with their governess, Jane Blaker, visiting art galleries and making extensive notes on the collections there.

家中没有明确的艺术收藏传统，但姐妹接受的教育为这类兴趣准备了条件。学校重视文化学习，她们又随家庭女教师旅行、参观画廊、详细记录藏品。这里的such pursuits回指艺术收藏一类的文化活动；作者强调兴趣可以通过教育和接触逐渐形成，并不一定来自家族收藏传统。

原文第3段

The sisters began to make regular art purchases from 1908, which roughly coincided with the dates of their inheritance. They took advice from various people, including the art dealer Hugh Blaker (the brother of Jane Blaker) and David Croal Thompson, who was also an art dealer. While it was long assumed that these men were largely responsible for the nature of the sisters' collection, it has recently been accepted that Gwendoline and Margaret retained a far more active role in the process.

从1908年起，她们开始规律购画，时间大致与继承遗产相近。两位艺术商提供建议，但对他们影响的理解后来发生了变化：过去常把收藏风格主要归于男性顾问，较新的看法则认为姐妹在选择中比人们原先承认的更主动。最后一句区分的是两种历史解释，并没有否定顾问确实提供过帮助。

原文第4段

The sisters' journals reveal their preference for Old Master** paintings. Yet they initially made very few attempts to secure any such works. While the sisters were wealthy in relative terms, their income was nothing compared to the fortunes of American art collectors of this period, such as J. Pierpont Morgan. Quite simply, high quality Old Master works were, if not beyond their means, then beyond what they were willing to pay for them. Instead, their early purchases were of the fashionable, safe variety, and included, for example, paintings by the French artist Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot.

日记显示姐妹喜欢欧洲早期大师的作品，可是最初很少购入。原因不是没有兴趣，而是她们虽富裕，与美国大收藏家的财力仍有差距。高质量作品即使并非完全买不起，也超过她们愿意支付的价格，所以早期购藏偏向当时流行、较稳妥的作品。Instead承接前面的现实限制，解释实际购买如何偏离个人偏好。

词语与搭配

a deep sense of social responsibility

强烈的社会责任感

sense of后接抽象名词，表示对某种责任或价值的内在意识；这里解释她们为什么把私人财富用于文化和慈善。

rigorously geared toward such pursuits

受到严格安排，以这类活动为培养方向

be geared toward强调设计或安排的方向；such pursuits承接前面的艺术收藏，不等于她们在校期间已经成为收藏家。

retained a far more active role

保有比过去认识中更积极主动的作用

retain表示保持，far修饰比较级more active，强调两种历史看法对姐妹参与程度的估计不同。

beyond their means

超出她们的财力

means在这里是经济能力，与紧接着的beyond what they were willing to pay区分：支付不起与不愿支付并不是一回事。

句子精读

While it was long assumed that these men were largely responsible for the nature of the sisters' collection, it has recently been accepted that Gwendoline and Margaret retained a far more active role in the process.

长期以来，人们一直认为这些男性在很大程度上决定了姐妹收藏的面貌；但最近人们开始认可，格温多琳和玛格丽特在这一过程中发挥了远比原先认为的更主动的作用。

While连接两种形成于不同时期的认识，带有对照和让步意味。两处it都是形式主语，真正的内容分别是后面的that从句。these men指上文两位艺术商；the nature of the collection指收藏的风格和构成；the process指收藏选择的过程。long assumed与recently accepted对比的不是谁先买画，而是历史认识怎样改变。

Quite simply, high quality Old Master works were, if not beyond their means, then beyond what they were willing to pay for them.

简单地说，优质的古典大师作品，即便没有超出她们的财力，也超出了她们愿意为之支付的价格。

主干是works were beyond...。插入的if not...then...意为即使不能说达到前一种程度，至少也达到了后一种程度；这里不能把两个限制都理解为已经确定。what they were willing to pay是名词性从句，指她们愿意支付的金额；them指大师作品。

读完讲解，可以把原文连起来再读一次；想保留的词句可使用已有收藏功能。
Why we need silence｜噪声风险与城市降噪未作答段落信息匹配 / 人物／特征匹配 · 3 段 · 341 词 · 4 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 21 页

原文与作答 · 分开滚动

AHumans are finely attuned to noise, and for good reason. From an evolutionary perspective, sounds give us vital information, helping us navigate the world and avoid danger. To help ensure loud or unexpected noises get the attention they deserve, our internal chemistry alters in response to them. Our blood pressure goes up, muscles tense and glands release hormones that prepare us for fight or flight. In the short term, this is a good thing. When we are exposed to too much noise over the long term, however, those responses can lead to a multitude of health issues, from sleep disturbance to even cardiovascular disease.

BThe World Health Organization has recently designated excessive noise as an 'underestimated threat' to public health, and has said that people living in cities such as Mumbai, Tokyo and Buenos Aires are being exposed to far more than the recommended 40 decibels of noise at night. A report from the European Environment Agency concluded that noise was an ongoing and widespread issue in Europe, with at least 1 in 5 people consistently exposed to levels considered harmful to health. 'There are no "earlids" that can protect your brain from noise,' says Nick Antonio, an acoustic consultant who has contributed to the British and international standards for noise.

CThe good news is that several cities have been working to turn the volume down. One of the first to do so was London. 'By providing recommendations for quieter buses, reducing noise from roads and also controlling noise from aircraft, they were able to make the city quieter,' says Antonio. Other cities have introduced noise-reducing road coatings, for instance, alongside greenery that muffles sound. Some solutions are more specific: Washington DC's ban on petrol-powered leaf blowers came into effect recently, while in New York City, legislation has been approved to fine people who modify their vehicles to make them noisier. 'People are seeing the benefits of these more quiet environments in their cities,' Antonio says. 'I expect we will see much more of this in the future.'

题目与作答

Q14–16：Which section contains the following information? 原选项A–G保留，本片段含A–C。Q23：Match the statement with the correct person, A–D. You may use any letter more than once.

共用选项 · 原题 14、15、16

  • A
  • B
  • C
  • D
  • E
  • F
  • G

14. examples of strategies to decrease the noise that the public are exposed to

15. data indicating the extent of the problem of excessive noise

16. a description of physiological changes in our bodies when we hear sudden noises

23. The trend towards creating quieter urban locations is likely to increase in the coming years.

  • A Nick Antonio
  • B Justin Feinstein
  • C Tai Dotan Ben-Soussan
  • D Eric Pfeifer

对照答案，回到证据

第 14 题 · C

C列举公交、道路、飞机以及禁令等多项策略；不是只说噪声有害的B。

quieter buses, reducing noise from roads and also controlling noise from aircraft

第 15 题 · B

extent看覆盖范围；1 in 5与城市夜间分贝限制构成具体数据证据。

at least 1 in 5 people consistently exposed to levels considered harmful to health

第 16 题 · A

blood pressure、muscles、glands是身体变化，不是社会影响。

Our blood pressure goes up, muscles tense and glands release hormones

第 23 题 · A

这句话属于Antonio的直接引语，预测降噪趋势继续增加。

I expect we will see much more of this in the future.

核对原答案页

材料精读 · 内容与词句

文章先解释人为什么对声音敏感，再区分短暂警觉的适应价值与长期噪声暴露的健康代价，最后转入城市治理。身体机制、公共健康风险和具体降噪行动形成连续关系。

A

A Humans are finely attuned to noise, and for good reason. From an evolutionary perspective, sounds give us vital information, helping us navigate the world and avoid danger. To help ensure loud or unexpected noises get the attention they deserve, our internal chemistry alters in response to them. Our blood pressure goes up, muscles tense and glands release hormones that prepare us for fight or flight. In the short term, this is a good thing. When we are exposed to too much noise over the long term, however, those responses can lead to a multitude of health issues, from sleep disturbance to even cardiovascular disease.

声音在进化中帮助人辨认环境和躲避危险，因此突然而响亮的声音会引起血压升高、肌肉紧张和激素释放，为战斗或逃跑做准备。短期内这种反应有保护作用；长期反复承受过量噪声，却可能与睡眠和心血管等健康问题相连。however标出评价变化，变化的关键在暴露的强度和持续时间，而不是所有声音都有害。

B

B The World Health Organization has recently designated excessive noise as an 'underestimated threat' to public health, and has said that people living in cities such as Mumbai, Tokyo and Buenos Aires are being exposed to far more than the recommended 40 decibels of noise at night. A report from the European Environment Agency concluded that noise was an ongoing and widespread issue in Europe, with at least 1 in 5 people consistently exposed to levels considered harmful to health. 'There are no "earlids" that can protect your brain from noise,' says Nick Antonio, an acoustic consultant who has contributed to the British and international standards for noise.

文中引用世界卫生组织和欧洲环境署的说法，将上一段的个体反应扩大为公共健康议题：一些城市的夜间噪声高于文中提到的建议值，欧洲也有相当数量的人持续处于有害噪声水平。声学顾问用没有earlids这一比喻说明，人不像闭眼那样能简单关闭听觉。这些数值与recently都是原文写作时期的描述，不代表实时更新的统计。

C

C The good news is that several cities have been working to turn the volume down. One of the first to do so was London. 'By providing recommendations for quieter buses, reducing noise from roads and also controlling noise from aircraft, they were able to make the city quieter,' says Antonio. Other cities have introduced noise-reducing road coatings, for instance, alongside greenery that muffles sound. Some solutions are more specific: Washington DC's ban on petrol-powered leaf blowers came into effect recently, while in New York City, legislation has been approved to fine people who modify their vehicles to make them noisier. 'People are seeing the benefits of these more quiet environments in their cities,' Antonio says. 'I expect we will see much more of this in the future.'

作者转向城市已经采取的改善措施：伦敦从公交、道路和飞机噪声入手，其他城市采用低噪声路面与绿化，还有城市针对吹叶机或人为改响车辆立法。段落从综合政策写到具体噪声来源，说明公共环境可以通过设计和管理改变。最后关于未来会有更多行动的说法是Antonio的期待，不是已经发生的事实。

词语与搭配

finely attuned to noise

对噪声非常敏感

be attuned to表示敏锐察觉或适应某种信号；finely加强感知的精细程度。

in response to them

作为对它们的反应

in response to引出反应的触发因素；them回指响亮或出乎意料的声音。

an ongoing and widespread issue

一个持续存在且影响广泛的问题

ongoing说明时间上的持续，widespread说明涉及范围大，两者从不同维度描述问题。

reducing noise from roads

减少来自道路的噪声

from说明噪声来源；这里属于城市治理措施之一，表达的是降低噪声，而非把所有道路移除。

greenery that muffles sound

能够减弱声音的绿化植被

muffle是使声音变低、变闷，不能理解为完全隔绝；that从句说明这里提到绿化的功能。

句子精读

When we are exposed to too much noise over the long term, however, those responses can lead to a multitude of health issues, from sleep disturbance to even cardiovascular disease.

然而，当我们长期暴露于过量噪声时，这些反应可能引发多种健康问题，从睡眠受扰，甚至到心血管疾病。

When从句同时限定过量噪声与长期暴露。those responses回指前文血压、肌肉和激素的变化；can lead to表示可能的后果，不是每次暴露都会产生疾病。from...to...列出不同程度的健康问题，however把短期保护作用与长期风险连接起来。

Some solutions are more specific: Washington DC's ban on petrol-powered leaf blowers came into effect recently, while in New York City, legislation has been approved to fine people who modify their vehicles to make them noisier.

一些措施更加具体：华盛顿特区对汽油动力吹叶机的禁令近期开始生效，而纽约市则已批准立法，对改装车辆使其更吵的人处以罚款。

冒号后给出两座城市的实例，while在此并列对照两项政策，并非说明同时发生。to fine交代立法的目的；who修饰people，to make them noisier说明改装造成的变化，them指车辆。recently以原文叙述时间为参照。

这篇材料里可用于写作的表达

reducing noise from roads

减少道路噪声

适合说明鼓励公共交通、步行或骑行可能带来的生活环境收益。需要具体写出减少何种车流或噪声源，不把交通方式改变等同于必然消除所有噪声。

用于写作：题目讨论鼓励替代交通与限制车辆使用；道路噪声是与车辆使用直接相关的生活环境理由。

noise from aircraft

飞机产生的噪声

可用于旅游活动对机场附近居民的影响，须说明航班增长这一具体联系；不能把所有旅游目的地的主要问题一律写成航空噪声。

用于写作：题目明确要求考虑旅游对当地居民与环境的影响；条件句把表达限定在航空活动增长的目的地。

读完讲解，可以把原文连起来再读一次；想保留的词句可使用已有收藏功能。
The World of Sugar｜劳动组织与行业权力未作答选词摘要填空 · 2 段 · 203 词 · 6 题 · 同篇原文另有裁切

真题 · Cambridge IELTS 21 Academic · PDF 第 26 页

原文与作答 · 分开滚动

原文第4段The World of Sugar is also a story of similarity and continuity in sugar cultivation. For example, imported labour has been used for much large-scale production. German beet fields employed Polish workers; Mexicans and many others, including Sicilians, were vital to US sugar production. Cane cutting, Bosma shows, remains a poorly paid and brutal business to this day in many places in the world. But as well as this, the book is about the continuity of the use of traditional methods on small farms. In the mid 20th-century, this type of sugar production dominated in South Asia and Latin America.

原文第5段This is also a history of capitalists and sugar dynasties, as well as corporations that in some cases have remained influential over very long periods. Great firms and great interests have had profound influence on the policies of states. In many places - not just the British Caribbean but Cuba and the Philippines too - a powerful sugar bourgeoisie played a major role in politics and their interests were consequently protected by trade barriers and subsidies. In the battle for control of the industry, it was inevitably the poor countries which came off worse. All this is explored by Bosma with wonderful subtlety and control.

题目与作答

  • B agricultural developments

对照答案，回到证据

第 31 题 · H

波兰人赴德、墨西哥人等赴美均是跨地迁移劳工，概括为migrant workers。

German beet fields employed Polish workers; Mexicans and many others, including Sicilians, were vital to US sugar production

第 32 题 · E

small farms与small-scale cultivation对应；F outdated带有落后评价，原文只说traditional。

traditional methods on small farms

第 33 题 · I

资本家、糖业家族与公司合并概括为powerful individuals and businesses。

a history of capitalists and sugar dynasties, as well as corporations

第 34 题 · A

policies of states和politics对应national governments，不是农业技术。

Great firms and great interests have had profound influence on the policies of states

第 35 题 · G

贸易壁垒与补贴是financial controls的实例，不能只靠相同词选项。

their interests were consequently protected by trade barriers and subsidies

第 36 题 · C

poor countries对应less wealthy nations，came off worse对应were penalised。

it was inevitably the poor countries which came off worse

核对原答案页

材料精读 · 内容与词句

这部分将糖业的连续性放在两个层面观察：劳动者的处境和传统生产方式延续，资本、企业与国家政策的关系也长期存在。书评由田间劳动转向政治经济，解释谁能够保护自己的利益，谁更容易承担代价。

原文第4段

The World of Sugar is also a story of similarity and continuity in sugar cultivation. For example, imported labour has been used for much large-scale production. German beet fields employed Polish workers; Mexicans and many others, including Sicilians, were vital to US sugar production. Cane cutting, Bosma shows, remains a poorly paid and brutal business to this day in many places in the world. But as well as this, the book is about the continuity of the use of traditional methods on small farms. In the mid 20th-century, this type of sugar production dominated in South Asia and Latin America.

德国甜菜业、美国糖业都使用跨境劳工，说明不同地区的规模生产有相似的劳动力来源。作者继而指出，在文中所说的许多地方，砍甘蔗仍是报酬低、劳动艰苦的工作。另一种连续性是小农传统方法的延续，20世纪中叶在南亚和拉丁美洲占重要地位。连续性既指劳动处境，也指生产形式，不能把两者缩成同一个现象。

原文第5段

原文第1段Studies using electrodes attached to the heads of sleepers have shown that when we sleep, we do so in two ways that alternate throughout the night. The first is rapid eye movement (REM) or active sleep. During this stage our eyes move, even though our eyelids are closed. Our muscles also twitch slightly, though they are largely paralysed so we don't hurt ourselves. In contrast, we also engage in non-REM sleep, during which we barely move at all. Most dream states, and certainly those with the most vivid dreams, happen during REM sleep.

原文第2段There's some evidence that other mammals may also dream. For example, researchers compared the brain patterns of rats running through a maze when awake with their brain patterns during REM sleep. They found the patterns were very similar and concluded that the sleeping rats were dreaming about going through the maze.

原文第3段But finding evidence of dreaming in non-mammals has proved more difficult. Their brains are very different from those of humans, and it can often be difficult to record their activity while they are sleeping. Recently, however, researchers succeeded in recording brain activity in sleeping pigeons. As in mammals, the recordings revealed both REM and non-REM sleep. Intriguingly, REM sleep activity was high in brain regions involved in processing visual information, especially images related to physical activities such as flying, which suggests that this may possibly be what the pigeons were dreaming about.

原文第4段That said, dreaming and REM sleep are unlikely to be universal in the animal kingdom. For example, sponges don't have brains, so they lack the machinery for dreaming. There are also some animals with unusual sleep patterns. These include whales and dolphins, which do not shut down their entire brain when they sleep, but only half of it, keeping the rest awake. They also show no sign of REM sleep, suggesting that they may only experience non-REM dreams, which are less vivid. This is surprising because we tend to think of whales and dolphins as having complex inner lives. It's thought that they don't experience REM sleep because during REM sleep animals are more vulnerable to extremes of temperature.

DThe Mapungubwe plateau has a very high number of carnivore animal remains and ivory splinters, suggesting that the skins of these large animals and ivory elephant tusks were accumulated, probably for trade with coastal areas reached by the Limpopo River. The presence of glass beads, almost certainly from India, indicate there was trade of some sort with other states on the coast who, in turn, traded with merchants travelling from India by sea. Mapungubwe also benefitted from locally-sourced copper and the gold trade as it passed from the kingdom of Great Zimbabwe (12-15th century), situated to the north of Mapungubwe, to the coastal city of Kosala. It is likely that trade links led to a strengthening of political authority in order to control and even monopolise these lucrative interregional connections.

EArchaeological discoveries reveal that pottery was produced on a scale large enough to suggest the presence of professional potters, and is another indicator of the prosperity of Mapungubwe society. Archaeological finds include spherical vessels with short necks, beakers, and bowls, many of which have decorative stamps. There are also ceramic discs, and whistles. In addition, cattle, sheep, and goat figurines, and small figures of highly stylised humans with elongated bodies and short limbs have been found. The figures may have been used in ceremonies as offerings to ancestors, but their precise function is not known. Other discoveries include small jewellery items made from locally sourced copper.

FBeautifully decorated artefacts made of gold have also been found at Mapungubwe. A type of decoration, found nowhere else except Great Zimbabwe, involved the crafting of gold into small rectangular sheets and carving geometrical patterns into it. These sheets were then used to cover wooden objects (which have not survived) using small tacks, also made of gold. One such object that has been discovered may have been a sceptre, while additional evidence of local gold-working is a rhinoceros figurine made from small hammered sheets, and thousands of small gold beads. These objects were all found at the royal burial site and date to c. 1150. They are the first known indicators that gold had an intrinsic value of its own (as opposed to that of a currency) in southern Africa.

GThe kingdom of Mapungubwe was already in decline by the late 13th century, probably because overpopulation placed too much stress on local resources, a situation that may have been brought to a crisis point by a series of droughts. Trade routes may also have shifted northwards. Certainly, the areas that now prospered were to the north, such as Great Zimbabwe.

The presence of glass beads, almost certainly from India, indicate there was trade of some sort with other states on the coast who, in turn, traded with merchants travelling from India by sea.
